papers.title: Prefrontal Glx reduction during the sleep transition is associated with sleep onset latency.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.summary: Used simultaneous polysomnography and magnetic resonance spectroscopy to test whether medial prefrontal cortex GABA and Glx changes associate with sleep onset latency, leveraging the first-night effect. Found that Glx decreased during wake-to-sleep transition in the undisturbed session, and greater Glx reductions correlated with shorter sleep onset latency, whereas GABA did not change or correlate with SOL.

papers.title: Sleep spindles stabilize human thalamocortical networks, inhibiting pathological disruptions.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Using multi-night intracranial EEG from 55 epilepsy patients, this study found bidirectional interactions between sleep spindles and interictal epileptiform discharges (IEDs): spindles were associated with IED suppression, while IEDs increased subsequent spindle probability. Nights with fewer IEDs showed more frequent, longer, and faster spindles, suggesting spindles stabilize thalamocortical networks against pathological disruptions.

papers.title: One night of closed-loop auditory stimulation during sleep enhances memory consolidation in patients with Alzheimer's Disease.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial of 37 patients with biomarker-confirmed early symptomatic Alzheimer's disease, one night of closed-loop auditory stimulation (CLAS) during sleep significantly improved overnight word-pair consolidation (Cohen's dz = 0.42, p = 0.04) and enhanced stimulation-evoked slow-wave and fast spindle activity without disrupting sleep architecture. This is the first demonstration that CLAS can modulate sleep electrophysiology and improve memory consolidation in AD.

papers.title: EEG correlates of sleep stages, sleep discrepancy, and insomnia: a comparative analysis of people with insomnia and healthy sleepers using spectral power and sample entropy.
papers.summary: This study compared EEG band power and sample entropy across sleep stages and sleep discrepancy conditions in 64 participants with insomnia and healthy sleepers, using mixed-effects modeling. EEG metrics strongly correlated with physiological sleep stages but did not reliably distinguish self-reported sleep perception within the same stage or consistently differentiate insomnia from controls; group differences included regional Delta power during wakefulness, increased sample entropy in REM sleep, and decreased Beta power during positive discrepancy.

papers.title: Integrated respirometry and metabolomics unveil circadian metabolic dynamics in Drosophila.
papers.summary: Combined high-resolution respirometry with LC-MS metabolomics to characterize respiratory and metabolic dynamics in Drosophila melanogaster under sleep and circadian perturbations. Found that short-sleep mutants had elevated metabolic rates and shifted fuel preferences, while clock mutant and constant darkness conditions caused widespread metabolic dysregulation and impaired redox homeostasis.

papers.title: Circadian temperature compensation is intrinsically linked with metabolism and redox signaling.
papers.summary: Investigated the mechanistic basis of circadian temperature compensation using genetic, imaging, and biochemical approaches. Found that intracellular redox sensing of metabolic rate is intrinsic to temperature compensation and conserved in bacterial and mammalian cells.

papers.title: Ovariectomy, but not moderate intermittent hypoxia, promotes respiratory instability and risk of obesity in adult female rats.
papers.summary: Tested the combined effects of ovariectomy and moderate intermittent hypoxia on respiratory, metabolic, cardiovascular, and neuroendocrine regulation in adult female rats. Found that ovariectomy increased apnoea frequency, respiratory instability, and ventilatory responses to oxygen, and promoted weight gain and HPA axis activation, but moderate intermittent hypoxia did not worsen these outcomes.

papers.title: Napping during night shift preserves normal neural activity in nurses with sleep deprivation: evidence from functional magnetic resonance imaging study.
papers.summary: Used resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging to examine how night-shift napping modulates neural activity in sleep-deprived nurses. Found that sleep deprivation reduced ALFF in frontal, temporal, insular, subcortical, and cerebellar regions and increased ALFF in occipital, sensorimotor, and parietal areas, while napping mitigated these disturbances.

papers.title: Implications of Wearable Sleep Health Technology for Cardiovascular Health Assessment and Interventions: A Narrative Review.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes literature on wearable sleep health technology for cardiovascular assessment and intervention, emphasizing device performance against polysomnography. It reports that wearable devices generally show high sensitivity but lower specificity for detecting sleep versus wake, with multisensor and EEG-based devices approaching polysomnography-level staging, and discusses implications for scalable sleep health measurement in cardiometabolic lifestyle interventions.

papers.title: Frontal midline theta reduction during attentional reconfiguration links local cortical dynamics to network-level connectivity changes.
papers.summary: Examined whether transient frontal midline theta (Fmθ) reduction during attentional reconfiguration reflects local cortical dynamics or network-level connectivity reorganization in 36 healthy adults performing a rule-switching 2-back task with EEG. Fmθ reduction was associated with parietal (not occipital) alpha suppression and with robust increases in long-range theta-band coordination, suggesting two partially dissociable processes.

papers.title: Environmental enrichment remodels brain structural and behavioral plasticity in restricted and repetitive C58 mouse models.
papers.summary: Used structural MRI and diffusion-weighted imaging to assess how environmental enrichment alters brain volumetry and microstructure in C58 mice (a model of restricted and repetitive behaviors) versus C57 controls. Enrichment promoted microstructural plasticity, notably altered fiber density, and these changes were linked to reductions in restricted and repetitive behaviors with strain- and sex-dependent effects.

papers.title: Circadian Norepinephrine Rhythm Regulates Outflow Facility and IOP in Rat Eyes.
papers.summary: Investigated the role of norepinephrine in circadian rhythms of intraocular pressure and conventional outflow facility in Brown-Norway rats using immunolabeling, ELISA, tonometry, perfusion, and OCT. Aqueous NE and IOP were higher and outflow facility lower during subjective night, effects abolished by tetrodotoxin, indicating clock-driven sympathetic activity that constricts distal drainage vessels.

papers.title: Effects of trazodone on polysomnographic sleep architecture in patients with depression and sleep disorders: a systematic review and exploratory meta-analysis.
papers.summary: Systematic review and exploratory meta-analysis of 8 studies (980 patients) assessing trazodone effects on polysomnographic sleep architecture in depression with sleep disorders. Trazodone increased total sleep time, sleep efficiency, and slow wave sleep proportion while reducing sleep latency and N2 proportion, without significant REM changes, but with more adverse events.

papers.title: Quantum machine learning for detection of sleep deprivation from EEG signals
papers.summary: This study applied Quantum Support Vector Machines and Hybrid Quantum Neural Networks to classify sleep-deprived versus well-rested states from resting-state EEG using spectral band power, band ratios, Hjorth parameters, and functional connectivity features encoded into quantum states. The Hybrid Quantum Neural Network achieved accuracies of 96.88% at the epoch level and 81.25% at the subject level, outperforming previously reported results.

papers.title: Personalised federated learning for Riemannian and Euclidean EEG decoding
papers.summary: The paper adapts personalised federated learning for two EEG decoders, Riemannian SPDNet and Euclidean EEGNet, by sharing a common trunk while each subject retains a personal head. Personalised SPDNet achieved higher accuracy than standard federated learning and centralised training, converged in fewer rounds, communicated fewer parameters, and outperformed all EEGNet configurations on two of three motor-imagery datasets.

papers.title: HRV-Based Respiratory-Rate Estimation in Older Adults: Error Modeling and Pilot Validation for Wearable Sleep Monitoring.
papers.summary: Validated heart-rate variability high-frequency (HF) spectral peak as a proxy for respiratory rate using a simulation study and pilot ECG validation in 10 older adults. Estimation was reliable at high SNR (MAE=0.46 bpm in simulation), but real-data accuracy was limited (4/10 achieved MAE≤2 bpm) due to non-respiratory HF oscillations, harmonic confusion, and breathing variability.

papers.title: Ubiquitin-conjugating Enzyme E2M Destabilizes Heat Shock Protein 70 and Mediates Sleep Deprivation-Induced Cognitive Impairment in Mice.
papers.summary: Using a mouse model of sleep deprivation, this study shows that UBE2M is upregulated in the hippocampus and directly interacts with HSP70, promoting its polyubiquitination and destabilization. Recombinant UBE2M aggravated cognitive impairment and increased hippocampal oxidative stress and pro-inflammatory cytokines, identifying the UBE2M/HSP70 axis as a link between sleep deprivation and cognitive decline.

papers.title: Sleep-neuroinflammation interactions in Alzheimer's disease: a systematic review of biomarker pathways.
papers.summary: This PRISMA-2020 systematic review synthesized 40 original studies examining the interplay between objectively measured sleep alterations, neuroinflammation, and Alzheimer's disease pathology. The evidence supports a biologically plausible, potentially bidirectional relationship in which sleep disruption is linked to glial activation and AD-related protein accumulation, but highlights gaps in integrating human sleep physiology, central inflammatory markers, and multimodal AD biomarkers, necessitating longitudinal and interventional studies.

papers.title: A Low-Cost Wearable Multimodal Brain Signal Acquisition System Integrating EEG and fNIRS for Depression Detection.
papers.summary: The paper presents a low-cost wearable system integrating EEG and fNIRS with conductive rubber electrodes for long-term brain monitoring. Validation experiments confirmed reliable signal acquisition, and in a depression detection test with 31 subjects, multimodal signals outperformed single modalities by 8.4% over EEG and 23.5% over fNIRS.

papers.title: Sleep deprivation as a multi-system physiological stressor: A review of shared mechanisms and clinical implications.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes evidence on systemic consequences of insufficient sleep across cognitive, immune, metabolic, cardiovascular, reproductive, and genomic systems. It identifies three recurring mechanisms—sympathetic/HPA hyperactivation, low-grade inflammation, and circadian/hormonal desynchronization—and concludes that sleep duration, regularity, quality, continuity, and circadian alignment should be treated as distinct clinical targets.

papers.title: Targeting the Medial Prefrontal Cortex with Transcranial Focused Ultrasound Alleviates Adolescent Sleep-Deprivation-Induced Persistent Postsurgical Pain in Adulthood.
papers.summary: Using a mouse model of adolescent sleep deprivation followed by adult plantar incision, this study identified medial prefrontal cortex glutamatergic (mPFCGlu) hypoactivity as a mediator of persistent postsurgical pain (PPSP). Transcranial focused ultrasound (TFUS) at 200 Hz activated mPFCGlu neurons, alleviated PPSP, and was shown mechanistically to engage TRPC5-dependent Homer1 signaling, restoring glutamatergic synaptic plasticity and normalizing gamma oscillations and spike-gamma phase locking.

papers.title: Associations Between Breast Milk Energy Intake, Infant Sleep Duration and Time Until Next Feed.
papers.summary: In 34 healthy breastfeeding mother-infant dyads, 24-hour feeding and sleep data were collected to test whether breast milk energy intake predicts subsequent infant sleep duration or time to next feed. Linear mixed-effects models found no significant associations between energy intake from preceding, lagged, or cumulative feeds and sleep duration or feeding intervals.

papers.title: Circadian rhythm disruption aggravates high-fat diet-induced NAFLD through gut microbiota alterations in mice.
papers.summary: This study investigated whether gut microbiota alterations contribute to circadian rhythm disruption (CRD)-associated worsening of high-fat diet (HFD)-induced non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) in mice. CRD exacerbated metabolic dysfunction, liver injury, and microbiota dysbiosis; fecal microbiota transplantation from HFD-LD donors partially reshaped the microbiota and attenuated several CRD-associated metabolic and hepatic abnormalities, supporting a contributory role of gut microbiota in CRD-aggravated NAFLD.

papers.title: Diurnal Insulin Clearance and Circadian Metabolic Gene Signatures in MASLD: Integrative Multi-Dataset Physiological and Transcriptomic Analysis.
papers.summary: Integrative analysis of human clamp datasets and transcriptomic data found that insulin clearance exhibits diurnal variation, with higher nighttime than daytime rates in healthy individuals and MASLD patients, and that MASLD is associated with reduced overall insulin clearance and altered expression of circadian and insulin clearance-related genes. These findings suggest a link between insulin clearance and circadian metabolic gene signatures in MASLD.

papers.title: Associations Between Sleep State Misperception and Emotional States in Middle-Aged Adults: A Community-Based Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional study of 32 middle-aged adults using self-reports and smartwatch actigraphy, sleep misperception was associated with emotional states: tension-anxiety, depression-dejection, and total mood disturbance correlated with sleep discrepancy, and sex, total mood disturbance, and self-rated health were significant predictors. Groups with subjective-objective sleep discrepancies had higher tension-anxiety and fatigue-inertia, suggesting sleep misperception as a potential indicator of psychological well-being.

papers.title: Multimodal machine learning model integrating electroencephalography, heart rate variability and clinical measures for distinguishing major psychiatric disorders.
papers.summary: This retrospective cohort study of 1035 patients developed multimodal machine learning models integrating EEG, heart rate variability, and clinical data to differentiate bipolar disorder, major depressive disorder, and schizophrenia. The multimodal CatBoost model achieved an AUROC of 0.776, outperforming unimodal approaches, with EEG connectivity features in delta, alpha, and gamma bands identified as important for discrimination.

papers.title: [Sleep alterations as a risk factor for cardiometabolic health: emerging evidence and clinical implications].
papers.summary: This review examines the pathophysiological mechanisms linking sleep deprivation to cardiovascular disease, emphasizing autonomic dysregulation, endothelial dysfunction, systemic inflammation, and neuroendocrine-metabolic alterations, and highlights circadian misalignment as an emerging risk factor. It concludes that sleep duration, quality, continuity, and circadian synchronization should be considered essential in clinical assessment and cardiovascular prevention.

papers.title: Multigenerational daytime-restricted feeding exacerbates irradiation-induced hepatic DNA damage and aging in mice.
papers.summary: This study established a multigenerational mouse model of daytime-restricted feeding (DRF) from F0 to F10 to examine hepatic DNA damage and aging. Multigenerational DRF disrupted circadian expression of DNA repair genes, and after 1 Gy X-ray irradiation, F10 mice showed increased γH2AX foci, elevated p21, and more senescent cells, indicating that persistent DRF sensitizes the liver to genotoxic stress and accelerates cellular senescence.

papers.title: Sleep deprivation exacerbates lens‑induced myopia in association with ERK/NF‑κB pathway activation.
papers.summary: Using guinea pig models of lens-induced myopia, this study found that sleep deprivation exacerbated myopia progression, as indicated by increased diopter and axial length, decreased retinal dopamine and tyrosine hydroxylase, and activation of the ERK/NF-κB pathway. Administration of the ERK1/2 inhibitor BVD-523 reversed these effects, suggesting ERK/NF-κB as a potential therapeutic target.

papers.title: Sleep Quality and Adherence to the Mediterranean Diet in Male Young Adults: An Exploratory Study Among Amateur Soccer Players, Physically Active Individuals, and Individuals with High Sitting Time.
papers.summary: This exploratory study compared self-reported sleep quality, Mediterranean diet adherence, and chronotype among 55 male young adults (amateur soccer players, physically active individuals, and those with high sitting time). Soccer players and physically active individuals had significantly lower Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index scores (better sleep quality) than individuals with high sitting time, while no significant group differences were found in Mediterranean diet adherence or chronotype.

papers.title: Sleep Deprivation Can Lead to Increased Physiologically Based Irritability in College Students.
papers.summary: This physiological study of 34 US undergraduate students examined the relationship between sleep deprivation and irritability during cognitive tasks with irritable stimuli, using heart rate measurements. Significant increases in heart rate during the Insoluble Puzzle task suggest that task duration and perceived reward blocking may induce irritability in sleep-deprived individuals, and the study provides a research model for future work on irritability.

papers.title: Metabolite-Related Evidence Linking Metabolic Measures to Patient-Reported Outcomes in Inflammatory Bowel Disease: A Critical Narrative Review.
papers.summary: This critical narrative review synthesized human studies linking metabolite-related measures to patient-reported outcomes in adult inflammatory bowel disease. It found candidate associations between metabolites (e.g., amino acids, lipids, bile acids, microbiota-derived signals) and fatigue or mood-related burden, but no human studies paired measured metabolites with sleep-, pain-, or urgency-specific patient-reported outcome measures, and no validated metabolite signature for patient-reported burden was identified.

papers.title: Always Connected, Not Always Well: The Moderating Role of Sleep Quality in the Relationship Between Nomophobia and Mental Health Among University Students in Saudi Arabia.
papers.journal: European journal of investigation in health, psychology and education
papers.summary: This cross-sectional survey of 980 Saudi university students used PLS-SEM to test associations between four nomophobia dimensions and depression, anxiety, and stress, and the moderating role of sleep quality. Losing Connectedness and Giving Up Convenience were consistently positively associated with all three mental health outcomes, while sleep quality selectively moderated some relationships (e.g., sleep quality × Not Being Able to Communicate on depression and anxiety).

papers.title: The circadian clock component OsRVE6a orchestrates daytime SA-JA signaling crosstalk to enhance rice defenses.
papers.summary: This study identifies the rice circadian clock component OsRVE6a as a regulator that coordinates salicylic acid (SA) and jasmonic acid (JA) defense signaling during daytime biotic stress. Daytime feeding by the small brown planthopper induces OsRVE6a, which activates JA signaling via OsCOI1a, suppresses OsNPR1 to alleviate SA-JA antagonism, and directly activates SA-responsive genes including OsWRKY20, which is essential for OsRVE6a-mediated resistance.

papers.title: Severe Myocardial Bridging Without Obstructive Coronary Artery Disease Presenting as Non-ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction: A Management Challenge in Sinus Bradycardia.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 53-year-old male with severe myocardial bridging of the mid-left anterior descending coronary artery causing non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction in the absence of obstructive coronary artery disease, complicated by sinus bradycardia. Cautious beta-blocker therapy with metoprolol was attempted and the patient remained asymptomatic with negative stress tests at one-year follow-up.

papers.title: Preparation of a Thermosensitive Chitosan-Sea Cucumber Peptide Hydrogel and Its Alleviating Effect on Acute Alcohol-Induced Dual Liver and Brain Injury in Mice.
papers.summary: The study fabricated a thermosensitive chitosan–sea cucumber peptide hydrogel (CS-SCP gel) that showed a phase transition at 35.7 °C and sustained peptide release (74.83% over 330 min), and tested it in Kunming mice with acute alcohol intoxication. In mice, the gel prolonged latency to drunkenness, shortened sleep/sobering time, reduced blood ethanol and transaminase/lipid levels, and attenuated alcohol-induced liver and brain injury via antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects.

papers.title: Neurological and Neuropsychiatric Manifestations of Pediatric Inflammatory Multisystem Syndrome (PIMS/MIS-C): A Narrative Review.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes current literature on neurological and neuropsychiatric manifestations of pediatric inflammatory multisystem syndrome (PIMS/MIS-C), reporting that such symptoms occur in roughly 12–27% of pediatric patients and include headache, encephalopathy, seizures, and psychiatric disturbances. It concludes that early recognition and immunomodulatory therapy are associated with favorable neurological recovery, but that evidence remains observational and heterogeneous.

papers.title: Prevalence and associated factors of burnout among postgraduate trainee physicians in Bangladesh: a multicentre cross-sectional study.
papers.summary: A multicentre cross-sectional study of 703 postgraduate trainee physicians in Bangladesh assessed burnout using the Abbreviated Maslach Burnout Inventory, finding an overall burnout prevalence of 70%. Multivariate logistic regression identified shorter sleep duration (<7 hours) as the only independent predictor of burnout (OR 1.83, 95% CI 1.25–2.69, p=0.002).

papers.title: Integrated Neurorehabilitation Including EEG-Neurofeedback for Unilateral Spatial Neglect After Right Thalamo-Mesencephalic Intracerebral Hemorrhage: A Case Report.
papers.summary: A case report describes a 70-year-old patient with unilateral spatial neglect after right thalamo-mesencephalic intracerebral hemorrhage who underwent a 3-week multidisciplinary neurorehabilitation program including 15 EEG-neurofeedback sessions. Post-treatment assessments showed improved cognitive scores (MoCA 20→24; FAB 8→12), reduced neglect severity (Catherine Bergego Scale 17→5), and reliable gains in functional independence, but the authors note that clinical improvement cannot be specifically attributed to neurofeedback because all interventions were concurrent.

papers.title: Wernicke Encephalopathy Secondary to Cannabinoid Hyperemesis Syndrome in a 15-Year-Old Male Patient: A Case Report.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 15-year-old male with chronic cannabis use who developed Wernicke encephalopathy (WE) secondary to cannabinoid hyperemesis syndrome (CHS)-induced thiamine deficiency. The patient presented with nystagmus, ataxia, and altered mentation, with normal brain MRI; empiric thiamine supplementation led to rapid clinical improvement and full neurologic recovery, highlighting that normal imaging does not exclude WE.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
